explanation: Curling a single finger to call someone over can come across as brusque, commanding, or rude in Germany - more like summoning a pet than a person - but it isn't the severe taboo it is in parts of Asia. Germans more commonly wave with an open hand or simply call out to the person.
local_tip: Wave with an open hand, palm toward the person, or just say their name, instead of curling a single finger to beckon them.

also_check.note: Beckoning with a single curled finger is considered very rude; an open hand with the palm down and fingers waved together is used instead.
Beckoning with a finger is seen as highly offensive and is even historically associated with calling animals; an open-hand, palm-down wave is the polite alternative.
Common among friends, but it can come across as rude or dismissive in formal settings; a verbal invitation is safer.
